cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this inventive RSC import, praising Tim Minchin's witty score and Matthew Warchus's dazzling direction. Some find it overstuffed or exhaustingly relentless, but most celebrate its dark Dahl humor and theatrical magic.

sg.ra: Shubert's orchestra rake is shallow, so the center aisle seats and rows in the low center (roughly E-L) give the cleanest unobstructed view without relying on being lifted over people's heads. Patrons repeatedly call out Row G center as 'the best seat in the house' and flag Row Q as the point where the mezzanine overhang starts to clip the very top of the stage.
sg.rr: A-R (front-to-mid); Q can start to feel the overhang

sg.ra: Orchestra Left sections include rush-priced partial-view seats — the trade is a clipped stage-right view for significantly lower pricing than center orchestra.
sg.rr: A-T (multiple reviews across the full front-to-rear span; rear rows marked partial view)

sg.ra: Front mezzanine center at the Shubert is the most-praised section in this dataset: patrons repeatedly call Row A 'best seats in the house' and note the mezzanine is unusually close to the stage because the house is wider than deep. The critical cutoff is explicit in the sourced Reddit advice — 'I wouldn't go much further back than row F in the mezz' — because the balcony overhang above starts clipping the top of the stage from roughly row G onward.
sg.rr: A-F (front rows unanimously recommended; avoid G+)

sg.ra: Skip at any price above deep-discount: Mezz Left Row A has a Shubert-specific hazard patrons repeatedly flag — a front rail / metal bar / banner that sits in the eye-line and requires shorter guests to dodge or sit unnaturally straight for the full runtime. Deep on the aisle side (row A27+) the proscenium box itself cuts off stage right, and the rider head-to-head with Mezzanine Right explicitly favors the opposite side here because 'a lot of action happens on the left side and I had to lean across.' Row B onward is tolerable but the front row — the only reason to pay premium — is the compromised row.
sg.rr: A-B (most photos); full section goes to row K

sg.ra: The padded velvet front-rail barrier on Mezz R Row A is a distinctive Shubert feature — patrons lean into it as a forearm rest rather than fight it. The section-specific tradeoff: Row B actually rates higher than Row A in direct rider comparisons here because the Shubert's aggressive mezz rise means Row B looks cleanly over the Row A patrons, so don't over-pay for A.

Shubert's balcony is the theater's weakest bucket per both riders and Reddit. The section-specific quirk: the balcony's front railing has a 'wide ledge' / light boxes that sit high enough to block the front of the stage — short patrons (≤5'4") are told to bring a cushion, and every rider reports leaning forward to see action downstage. Combine that with the 'steeply raked' upper tier and patrons describe it as 'watching the show in miniature.'

The front row of side balcony is the Shubert's genuine value play — a single Mockingbird patron posted 'Definitely worth $69' four consecutive times across A3-A9, and a Hell's Kitchen rider describes Balcony Row A as 'felt more like a front mezzanine' because it isn't yet steep there. The tradeoff unique to this section: deep-left seats (A25/27) hit a hard partial-view wall, and Row B onward sits behind a railing multiple patrons flag as 'very in the way.' Buy A, not B.
sg.rr: A (front row only; rows B+ get worse sight lines and railing obstruction)
